subject: FintechCo — Post-demo performance SLOs & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Gupta <rajiv@fintechco.com>; Claire Summers <claire@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: FintechCo — Post-demo performance SLOs & next steps
Attachments: slo-checklist.csv (CSV)

Hi Rajiv / Claire —

Thanks again for the demo time yesterday — really appreciated the walkthrough of your chat flows and the high-throughput reconciliation use case. Per our conversation, I pulled together a short SLO checklist (attached) and a proposed mutual action plan to validate performance against your targets. Can you confirm the items below and add any missing constraints? Once we have clarity on the SLOs we’ll schedule a performance run and share results + a recommended deployment config.

Key items we discussed (please confirm numbers below):
- Target latency: p50 first-token <= 200ms, p95 first-token <= 400ms (end-to-end generation for median requests)
- Throughput: sustained 50 requests/sec across peak window; burst to 200 req/s for 5 minutes
- Concurrency: typical 10–25 concurrent active users; peak 40 concurrent users
- Streaming: yes — partial-token streaming required for the UI spinner/UX (must start streaming within 150ms of first-token generation)
- Context length: 8k tokens typical; occasional 32k token archival lookups
- Output size: median 150 tokens, 95th percentile 2k tokens

Next steps / MAP items:
1) Confirm/adjust the SLO targets above and return the completed slo-checklist.csv
2) Share a representative perf dataset and a short list of test prompts
3) Provide a scoped test API key or enable a test tenant for Redwood perf runs
4) Confirm target model variant (latency-optimized vs quality-optimized)

Proposed timeline: we can run a perf test within 3 business days of receiving the dataset and test access.

I’ll follow up internally on the perf harness and a proposed test plan. Thanks — looking forward to the details.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: fintechco-performance-requirements.xlsx (Excel)

Hi Marissa —

Great recap — I filled out the checklist and attached a brief requirements workbook. A few clarifications / firm numbers from our side:

- Latency: our product team expects end-to-end p50 <= 220ms and p95 <= 500ms for interactive chat (first-token); for batch inference (background reconciliations) p95 <= 1.2s is acceptable.
- Throughput: sustained 60 req/s during daily ingestion windows; allow headroom for 180 req/s burst for up to 10 minutes during batch runs.
- Concurrency: ~30 concurrent agents during peak; occasional spikes to 80 during batch rollouts.
- Streaming: required for interactive chat. We rely on progressive partial responses for UX. First partial should arrive within 200ms of request acceptance.
- Context length: baseline 8k, with historical lookups up to 32k for certain reconciliation flows.
- Outputs: median 120 tokens; 95th 1.8k tokens; some bulk jobs produce up to 8k tokens (will flag separately).

Security note: our InfoSec team will follow up with a short questionnaire (SOC2 / encryption at rest, KMS). We’d like a perf run before procurement sign-off; can Redwood provide a scoped test environment?

Happy to jump on a short sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Director of Platform Engineering | FintechCo
rajiv@fintechco.com

To: Rajiv Gupta <rajiv@fintechco.com>; Claire Summers <claire@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo performance SLOs & next steps

Thanks Rajiv — this is exactly what we needed, and the workbook is super helpful. Quick clarifications based on your numbers:

- We can prioritize interactive chat latency (first-token) for the perf run and benchmark batch jobs separately.
- Streaming: we’ll verify first-byte streaming time (target <200ms) and add a p95 streaming chunk latency metric to the checklist.
- Concurrency: we’ll test at 30 concurrent agents and run a spike test to 80 for a short window to validate degradation characteristics.
- Model variant: can you indicate whether you prefer a latency-optimized / quantized variant (lower cost, lower quality) or quality-optimized (higher compute, higher quality)? If undecided, we’ll run both in the perf window and compare cost vs latency.

Next steps I’ll own:
- Schedule a perf run (internal ETA: within 3 business days after we receive dataset & test access).
- Share test plan + expected metrics (link below).
- Create HubSpot activity and attach the completed checklist to the deal.

Action items for FintechCo:
- Return completed slo-checklist.csv (attached) with any additional constraints (security, region).
- Provide a small representative prompt set + sample payloads and estimated peak windows.
- Grant test ingress (scoped API key OR temporary test tenant).

I’ve created a perf run placeholder here: https://redwood.app/perf-runs/FIN-1234. Once we have your dataset and test access we’ll lock timing — please indicate ideal days/times for a run.

If it helps, we can run an initial single-model quick test (2–3 hours) to validate streaming characteristics before a full-scale throughput test.

Best,
Marissa

Date: 2028-04-14T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: FintechCo — Post-demo performance SLOs & next steps
Attachments: perf-test-plan.pdf (PDF)

Marissa / Dylan —

Saw Rajiv’s numbers — looks feasible. Notes from infra side:
- For the interactive chat SLOs (p95 <= 500ms first-token) we should run against the latency-optimized variant on Dedicated or a low-latency hosted pool. That config gives us the best chance to meet <500ms at 30 concurrent agents.
- For batch flows that need higher throughput / larger context, we’ll use a throughput-optimized config and run multi-node parallel workers. Expect different cost profiles — we’ll capture cost vs latency in the perf report.
- Test harness: I’ll own the perf harness and create a run plan (attached). Plan: start with single-model streaming validation (2 hours), then full throughput spike tests (6 hours) with gradual ramp to 180 req/s and an 80-concurrency spike window.
- Need from FintechCo: scoped test API key, representative payloads (JSON), and an indicator of peak timezone (to schedule a run during their traffic window).

I created Jira INFRA-982 to track the perf run tasks and will post results + graphs there.

Will coordinate with Marissa to propose exact run dates once we have the dataset and test access.

—Aditya
Senior Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
